method: Reviewed the complete scope lesson against the local historical data ledger, the current P5 runner and RUNBOOK, the project tool registry, and the cost-model scenario. Clarified that the project has one predeclared smoke case, while each task is bounded and the runner advances one wake-up per invocation; the runbook allows sequential wake-ups and a new synthetic task with a fresh idempotency key. Ran both offline lesson verifiers and P5 live-runner/release-candidate unit tests. No provider or external network call was made.

observations.trace: The scope check passes 9/9 and the preserved issue-scoped contract passes 5/5. The example matches the three project tools and detects an added refund_order tool. P5 live-runner and release-candidate tests pass 35 tests plus 13 subtests. Historical totals 678/1326/2623/4945 and the approximately 54.7 input-token difference match docs/DATA.md; the 8/8-per-group tool probe remains an unreproducible summary. The approximately 62% figure is a fixed local scenario, not a provider bill. Production build generated 404 pages; Pagefind indexed 404 pages / 15,462 words. Light/dark full-page renders are 1300x8676, article 792px, viewport/document scroll width 1300px, Mermaid rendered; sole browser console error is favicon 404.

limitations: No real provider call, external sink delivery, production authorization, persistence behavior, or global live-run quota was exercised in this review.
The 2026-10-08 tool-count and 8/8 selection summaries lack raw request/response artifacts, full usage, question mapping, and scorer; they were not reproduced.
The fixed smoke test case can be resumed through multiple wake-ups and re-created as a new task under the runbook; each task is bounded but the project does not declare a global invocation cap.
